source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: According to the lecture, what is a skill, structurally speaking?

options.text: A single system prompt that gets appended to every conversation
options.feedback: A system prompt is one flat block of text added to every turn. A skill is the opposite: most of it, including any scripts or reference files, only loads when the task actually calls for it.

options.text: A subdirectory of instructions for an agent, often bundled with scripts and reference files
options.feedback: This is close to how the lecture put it: a skill is a subdirectory of instructions for the agent, and it can carry along scripts and reference files that get used only when the task needs them.

options.text: A separate, fine-tuned copy of the underlying model
options.feedback: Fine-tuning changes the model's weights themselves, which takes retraining. A skill changes nothing about the model -- it is just files that tell an existing model how to approach a task.

options.text: A plugin that only works if it is written in the same programming language as the harness
options.feedback: Skills are portable specifically because they are not tied to one programming language or vendor. Requiring a language match would defeat the point of a format any compatible harness can read.
